correctness.rationale: Directly checked all dimensions of the real Fourier plus radial decomposition. PBH restrictions reduce exactly to sin(2πjd/m), the gcd congruence, the alternating-mode parity condition, and the determinant of a three-row affine unit-circle matrix. All minima and placement classifications follow for every m>=3 and t>0. Exact finite modular tests on 3548 pair cases and 1146 triple cases corroborate but do not replace the analytic proof; rational-rank loss is never inferred solely from finite-field rank loss.

originality.rationale: The claim is not the standard PBH criterion, known rim Fourier spectrum, or existing wheel adjacency spectral formula. It uniquely combines coupling-dependent collisions with complete pair and triple placement arithmetic and parity-sensitive counts; no accessible inspected paper or indexed record was found to state or imply that combined classification. Spectral predecessor is expressly credited, and residual literature/priority risk remains.
residual_risks: The method combines standard Fourier eigenpairs and PBH, so an unlocated general theorem about arrow-bordered-circulant controllability could dominate the classification.
The highly relevant Florek–Marlewski wheel spectrum makes this a close derivative, though its documented claims are spectral only.

Indexed research-record full manuscripts for the cycle-sensor and wheel-polytope comparisons were not retrieved; their summaries support distinction of objects but not a whole-document negative claim.
Unindexed specialty wheel controllability papers and alternative follower-state models may yield equivalent or stronger conclusions.

value.rationale: The sharp discontinuity in minimum control number at selected spoke couplings is a structurally meaningful control-design boundary. The theorem solves the exact minimum leader count and gives every optimal pair and triple for all m>=3, with explicit mod-arithmetic and parity tests and placement enumerations. This is an intrinsic optimal-design classification rather than a minor numerical gain or a restatement of spectral eigenvalues.
